statements.status_notes: sha256crypt and sha512crypt through 0.6 allow attackers to cause a denial of service (CPU consumption) because the algorithm's runtime is proportional to the square of the length of the password.
statements.impact_statement: glibc sha256crypt/sha512crypt algorithmic-complexity denial-of-service issue (CPU cost proportional to the square of password length), which Ubuntu has marked Ignored as architectural (will never be fixed without migrating hash schemes). Affects crypt(3) password hashing, which the JVM never calls.

statements.status_notes: Calling wordexp with WRDE_REUSE in conjunction with WRDE_APPEND in the GNU C Library version 2.0 to version 2.42 may cause the interface to return uninitialized memory in the we_wordv member, which on subsequent calls to wordfree may abort the process.
statements.impact_statement: The uninitialized-memory return needs a process that calls glibc's wordexp() with both WRDE_REUSE and WRDE_APPEND. An inspection of every ELF binary and shared library in the shipped image, including the JRE's native libraries, found none that imports wordexp; the symbol appears only in libc.so.6 itself. lpm is a statically linked Go binary, so the vulnerable wordexp() path is never reached by Liquibase Secure. Fixed in Ubuntu glibc 2.35-0ubuntu3.13 (jammy; Liquibase Secure 5.0.0 and 5.0.1 shipped 2.35-0ubuntu3.10 and 2.35-0ubuntu3.11) and 2.39-0ubuntu8.7 (noble; Liquibase Secure 5.0.2 and 5.0.3 shipped 2.39-0ubuntu8.6); Liquibase Secure 5.1.0 and later ship 2.39-0ubuntu8.7 or newer.

statements.status_notes: The GNU C Library regcomp function from versions 2.4 through 2.41 can double-free memory if an earlier allocation fails, which may permit buffer manipulation depending on the constructed regular expression.
statements.impact_statement: The vulnerable regcomp() double free needs a process that compiles a regular expression through glibc after an earlier allocation failure. An inspection of the shipped image found that neither the JVM nor any JRE native library imports regcomp; Java regular expressions are implemented in java.util.regex, not in glibc. The only importers are OS utilities such as bash, grep, tar and wget, which are either not part of the runtime path or, in the case of the bash entrypoint, do not use regular-expression matching. lpm is a statically linked Go binary. Fixed in Ubuntu glibc 2.35-0ubuntu3.11; only Liquibase Secure 5.0.0 (jammy, 2.35-0ubuntu3.10) shipped an affected build.

statements.status_notes: Passing an excessively large alignment to memalign, posix_memalign, or aligned_alloc in the GNU C Library can overflow internal arithmetic and lead to heap corruption when the caller controls both the size and the alignment values.
statements.impact_statement: The vulnerable arithmetic in memalign, posix_memalign and aligned_alloc is triggered only when a caller passes an attacker-controlled, exceptionally large alignment. An inspection of the shipped image found that libjvm.so imports posix_memalign and libmlib_image.so imports memalign, but both pass fixed alignments chosen by the runtime (page and cache-line sizes), never a value derived from user input; no other process in the runtime path uses the memalign family, and lpm is a statically linked Go binary. Fixed in Ubuntu glibc 2.35-0ubuntu3.13 (jammy) and 2.39-0ubuntu8.7 (noble); Liquibase Secure 5.0.0 through 5.0.3 shipped affected builds, and Liquibase Secure 5.1.0 and later ship 2.39-0ubuntu8.7 or newer.

statements.status_notes: Calling getnetbyaddr or getnetbyaddr_r in the GNU C Library with a configured DNS backend for networks and a zero-valued network query can leak stack contents to the configured DNS resolver.
statements.impact_statement: The stack leak needs a process that calls getnetbyaddr() or getnetbyaddr_r() while nsswitch.conf routes the networks database to DNS. Neither condition holds in the Liquibase Secure image: an inspection found that no JRE native library imports the getnetbyaddr family (the only importers are the getent utility and the perl interpreter, neither of which runs at runtime), and /etc/nsswitch.conf configures networks: files with no dns backend. lpm is a statically linked Go binary. Fixed in Ubuntu glibc 2.35-0ubuntu3.13 (jammy) and 2.39-0ubuntu8.7 (noble); Liquibase Secure 5.0.0 through 5.0.3 shipped affected builds, and Liquibase Secure 5.1.0 and later ship 2.39-0ubuntu8.7 or newer.

statements.status_notes: Passing an effectively empty string to the ",ccs=" syntax extension of the mode argument in the fopen function in the GNU C Library version 2.45 or earlier may result in a heap buffer overflow when the mode string input to the function is attacker controlled. This usage pattern is not seen in applications in common GNU/Linux distributions.
statements.impact_statement: This heap buffer overflow requires an application to call glibc's fopen function with an attacker-controlled mode string containing an effectively empty ",ccs=" syntax extension; the file path is irrelevant. Every fopen call in the Temurin 21 JRE passes a constant mode string ("r", "rb", "w", "a" and similar), Java-level file I/O uses open(2) rather than fopen, the bash entrypoint has no user-controlled fopen mode, and lpm is a static Go binary that does not link glibc. No shipped program builds an fopen mode string from external input. The same glibc 2.39 source builds libc6, libc-bin and locales, and the reasoning applies to each.

statements.status_notes: Calling strfmon and strfmon_l in the GNU C Library version 2.38 to 2.44 can write past the end of the caller-supplied output buffer when a conversion uses right-justified width padding. At the time of publication, no network-facing application impact is known.
statements.impact_statement: This glibc flaw is reachable only through application calls to strfmon or strfmon_l with a vulnerable right-justified width-padding pattern. The Liquibase Secure image inherits the OS package from eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (`docker/Dockerfile:2`) and the container entrypoint execs only the Liquibase CLI (`docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8`, `docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119`). A focused grep across the runtime Dockerfiles, entrypoint scripts, and application source found no references to strfmon or strfmon_l, so the vulnerable API path is not reachable from the stock Liquibase Secure runtime.

statements.status_notes: Calling tdelete on a sufficiently deep tree in the GNU C Library version 2.1 to 2.44 may write one pointer past the end of an alloca-allocated array on the stack, which may crash the application. No affected application in common distributions has been identified.
statements.impact_statement: This glibc flaw requires an application to use tsearch/tdelete on a very deep tree. The Liquibase Secure image inherits the OS package from eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (`docker/Dockerfile:2`) and the container entrypoint execs only the Liquibase CLI (`docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8`, `docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119`). A focused grep across the runtime Dockerfiles, entrypoint scripts, and application source found no references to tsearch or tdelete, so the vulnerable API path is not reachable from the stock Liquibase Secure runtime.

statements.status_notes: The iconv() function in the GNU C Library versions 2.43 and earlier may crash due to an assertion failure when converting inputs from the IBM1390 or IBM1399 character sets, which may be used to remotely crash an application. This vulnerability can be trivially mitigated by removing the IBM1390 and IBM1399 character sets from systems that do not need them.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports libc-bin 2.39-0ubuntu8.7, below Ubuntu's fixed 2.39-0ubuntu8.8, but this issue requires an application to process IBM1390 or IBM1399 encoded input through glibc's iconv conversion path. The stock Liquibase Secure runtime is the Liquibase Java CLI, and a review of its build and runtime path found no references to iconv or those IBM1390 or IBM1399 code pages.

statements.status_notes: Calling gethostbyaddr or gethostbyaddr_r with a configured nsswitch.conf that specifies the library's DNS backend in the GNU C Library version 2.34 to version 2.43 could, with a crafted response from the configured DNS server, result in a violation of the DNS specification that causes the application to treat a non-answer section of the DNS response as a valid answer.
statements.impact_statement: glibc gethostbyaddr/gethostbyaddr_r DNS-response-parsing bug (CWE-125), exploitable when a crafted response from the configured DNS resolver causes the application to treat a non-answer section as a valid answer. Liquibase Secure only performs a reverse-DNS lookup through this path via NetUtil.getLocalHostName() (core/liquibase-standard/src/main/java/liquibase/util/NetUtil.java), which resolves the container's own local address -- never an attacker-supplied or remote address -- and caches the result in a static field after the first call. It is used purely for cosmetic/ attribution fields (DATABASECHANGELOGLOCK owner in LockDatabaseChangeLogGenerator, license/run-context tracking, drift report hostname), never for access control or trust decisions. Exploitation therefore requires a compromised or MITM'd DNS resolver already configured and trusted by the deployment (via /etc/resolv.conf and nsswitch.conf's "dns" hosts backend) -- not an arbitrary remote attacker. Version check: the currently published liquibase/liquibase-secure:5.2.2 image ships libc-bin 2.39-0ubuntu8.9 (already >= the 2.39-0ubuntu8.8 fix); tags 5.2.1 down to 5.0.2 ship 2.39-0ubuntu8.7 or 8.6 (unfixed by version), and 5.0.1 ships an older 2.35-0ubuntu3.11 base entirely, so the reachability argument (not the package version) is what covers the whole published tag range.

statements.status_notes: Calling gethostbyaddr or gethostbyaddr_r with a configured nsswitch.conf that specifies the library's DNS backend in the GNU C library version 2.34 to version 2.43 could result in an invalid DNS hostname being returned to the caller in violation of the DNS specification.
statements.impact_statement: glibc gethostbyaddr/gethostbyaddr_r invalid-hostname bug (CWE-20/ CWE-88), where a crafted DNS response can cause an invalid hostname to be returned to the caller. Liquibase Secure's only reverse-DNS call site is NetUtil.getLocalHostName() (core/liquibase-standard/src/main/java/liquibase/util/NetUtil.java), resolving the container's own local address (never a remote or attacker-supplied one), cached after the first lookup, and used only for cosmetic attribution fields (DATABASECHANGELOGLOCK owner, license/run-context tracking, drift report hostname) -- never parsed, executed, or used in an authorization decision, which also bounds the CWE-88 argument-injection concern this CVE separately flags for callers that shell out with the returned hostname. Exploitation requires a compromised or MITM'd DNS resolver already trusted by the deployment. Version check: same as CVE-2026-4437 -- only the currently published 5.2.2 tag ships a fixed libc-bin (2.39-0ubuntu8.9); 5.2.1 down to 5.0.1 remain on an unfixed build, so this reachability argument, not package version, is what covers the whole published tag range.

statements.status_notes: The deprecated functions ns_printrrf, ns_printrr and fp_nquery in the GNU C Library version 2.2 and newer fail to enforce the caller-supplied buffer length, and can result in an out-of-bounds write when printing TSIG records.
statements.impact_statement: This CVE affects deprecated glibc resolver-printing functions used for TSIG record formatting. Liquibase Secure's stock runtime is the Liquibase Java CLI, and a source review found no references to ns_printrrf, ns_printrr, fp_nquery, or TSIG processing in the product runtime path. libc-bin is inherited from the base image only, so the vulnerable glibc function path is not reachable from Liquibase Secure.

statements.status_notes: Calling the scanf family of functions with a %mc (malloc'd character match) conversion in the GNU C Library version 2.7 to 2.43 with an explicit field width greater than 1024 can result in a one byte heap buffer overflow.
statements.impact_statement: This glibc flaw is reachable only through a scanf-family call that uses the %mc conversion with an explicit field width above 1024 on attacker-controlled input. The Liquibase Secure image runs the Liquibase Java CLI on a Temurin JRE plus the lpm helper, which is a statically linked Go binary that does not use glibc at all. An inspection of the shipped image found no %mc scanf directive in the JVM, the JRE native libraries, the shell entrypoint or any OS binary, so the vulnerable glibc pattern is not reachable from Liquibase Secure.

statements.status_notes: Calling the ungetwc function on a FILE stream with wide characters encoded in a character set that has overlaps between its single byte and multi-byte character encodings, in the GNU C Library version 2.43 or earlier, may result in an attempt to read bytes before an allocated buffer, potentially resulting in unintentional disclosure of neighboring data in the heap, or a program crash.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports libc-bin 2.35-0ubuntu3.10, below Ubuntu's fixed 2.35-0ubuntu3.14, but this issue requires an application to call glibc's ungetwc wide-character pushback path on a FILE stream using a character set with overlapping single-byte and multibyte encodings. Liquibase Secure's stock runtime path is the Java CLI, and a review of its build and runtime flow found no references to ungetwc or related native wide-character stream handling in the product runtime path.

statements.status_notes: The deprecated functions ns_printrrf, ns_printrr and fp_nquery in the GNU C Library version 2.0.1 to version 2.43 fail to validate the RDATA content against the RDATA length in a DNS response when processing A6, CERT, LOC, TKEY or TSIG records, which may allow an attacker to craft a DNS response, causing a target application to crash or read uninitialized memory.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports libc-bin 2.35-0ubuntu3.10, below Ubuntu's fixed 2.35-0ubuntu3.14, but this issue affects deprecated glibc debugging helpers for printing DNS record data rather than the resolver path itself. Liquibase Secure's stock runtime is the Liquibase Java CLI, and a source review found no references to ns_printrrf, ns_printrr, fp_nquery, or TSIG-related record-printing in the product runtime path.

statements.status_notes: Calling wordexp with WRDE_APPEND in the GNU C Library version 2.0 to version 2.43 can cause the interface to return invalid memory in the we_wordv member, which on subsequent calls to wordfree may abort the process.
statements.impact_statement: This flaw requires an application to call glibc's wordexp function with the WRDE_APPEND flag. Neither the JVM nor the container's bash entrypoint calls wordexp; this is a C-language shell-word-expansion API that Liquibase Secure's Java and bash-only runtime path never invokes.

statements.status_notes: When expanding paths that begin with a tilde followed by a username, glibc's parse_tilde allocates the extracted username on the stack with strndupa based on untrusted input length. If an application passes attacker-controlled input to wordexp, an excessively long username can exhaust stack space and trigger a stack clash.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports libc-bin 2.35-0ubuntu3.10, below Ubuntu's fixed 2.35-0ubuntu3.15, but this flaw requires an application to pass attacker-controlled input into glibc's wordexp path-expansion API. The stock Liquibase Secure runtime is the Liquibase Java CLI behind a bash-based entrypoint, and a source review found no references to wordexp or WRDE_APPEND in the container build or runtime path.

statements.status_notes: Converting crafted SHIFT_JISX0213 input to UCS-4 or the internal wide character encoding, for example with iconv, in the GNU C Library version 2.3 to 2.44 may result in the converter making no progress, causing the calling application to hang.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports libc-bin 2.35-0ubuntu3.10, below Ubuntu's fixed 2.35-0ubuntu3.15, but this issue requires an application to feed attacker-controlled SHIFT_JISX0213 data through glibc's iconv conversion path with a small enough output buffer to split a two-code-point decode. Liquibase Secure's stock runtime path is the Java CLI, and a review of its build and runtime flow found no references to iconv or SHIFT_JISX0213 processing. The vulnerable glibc conversion path is not reachable from Liquibase Secure.

statements.status_notes: Converting crafted EUC_JISX0213 input to UCS-4 or the internal wide character encoding, for example with iconv, in the GNU C Library version 2.3 to 2.44 may result in the converter making no progress, causing the calling application to hang.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports libc-bin 2.35-0ubuntu3.10, below Ubuntu's fixed 2.35-0ubuntu3.15, but this issue requires an application to feed attacker-controlled EUC_JISX0213 data through glibc's iconv conversion path with a small enough output buffer to split a two-code-point decode. Liquibase Secure's stock runtime path is the Java CLI, and a review of its build and runtime flow found no references to iconv or EUC_JISX0213 processing. The vulnerable glibc conversion path is not reachable from Liquibase Secure.

statements.status_notes: Initializing the DNS stub resolver from an /etc/resolv.conf file, or a LOCALDOMAIN environment variable, whose search list contains a domain of roughly 200 characters or more in the GNU C Library version 2.26 to 2.44 results in an assertion failure which aborts the process. The resolver truncates the search list when copying it into the fixed-size _res.defdname buffer, then asserts that the copy is consistent with the full configuration. The consistency check compared against the wrong size and did not handle a first entry that does not fit, so a correctly truncated list failed the assertion. Any process that resolves names through the library is affected, including long-running processes that reload /etc/resolv.conf on the next query after it changes. Search domains are commonly written to /etc/resolv.conf from data received over DHCP or from a VPN server, so an attacker on the local network may be able to trigger this without privileges on the target system, subject to validation by the network configuration software.
statements.impact_statement: glibc DNS stub resolver assertion-abort issue when /etc/resolv.conf or LOCALDOMAIN contains a ~200+ character search-list domain. Requires attacker control of the container's DNS configuration; not remotely triggerable against this image.

statements.status_notes: A time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition in the dynamic loader (ld.so) of the GNU C Library (glibc) versions 2.14 through 2.44 allows a local attacker to escalate privileges. When expanding $ORIGIN in DT_RPATH for setuid/setgid (AT_SECURE) programs, glibc validates the lexically normalized search path against the trusted directories but then opens the raw, un-normalized path. On systems where fs.protected_hardlinks is disabled, an attacker who hard-links such a program and swaps a path component for a symbolic link can make the loader load an attacker-controlled shared object.
statements.impact_statement: Exploitation needs a setuid or setgid binary whose DT_RPATH uses $ORIGIN, plus a local attacker able to hard-link it and win a race. None of the setuid/setgid binaries shipped in the Liquibase Secure image (su, passwd, mount, chsh and the other shadow and util-linux tools) contain $ORIGIN at all, and the container runs Liquibase as the unprivileged liquibase user. fs.protected_hardlinks, enabled by default on major distributions, also blocks the hard-link step.

statements.status_notes: The nscd service in the GNU C Library 2.3.4 onwards may crash due to a stack overflow when a malicious DNS server returns too large a response for a DNS query, resulting in degraded DNS resolution for the system. Exploitation of this bug needs a system that has nscd enabled and using an untrusted DNS server for name resolution, with the compromised DNS server being capable of processing records large enough to result in a stack overflow in an nscd thread stack. During experimentation, bind 9 was unable to handle large records, but that could change in future or with a different name server. In typical installations, nscd is executed in an isolated context as its own user without a shell, due to which any compromise of that service is isolated. There is a remote possibility of nscd cache corruption if an attacker manages to get the stack pointer into a desired point in the heap, potentially resulting in other caches in nscd being overwritten with corrupt data through the stack overflow, until the buggy code path eventually results in a crash. Finally, a crash in nscd may result in performance degradation when resolving names, but it does not result in a denial of service.
statements.impact_statement: glibc nscd stack-overflow crash when a malicious DNS server returns an oversized response. Requires nscd running against an untrusted DNS server; this minimal image runs no nscd process at all.

statements.status_notes: A stack-based buffer overflow in the dynamic loader (ld.so) of the GNU C Library (glibc) versions 2.14 through 2.44 allows a local attacker to crash or corrupt the memory of setuid/setgid (AT_SECURE) programs. When such a program's DT_RPATH or DT_RUNPATH begins with $ORIGIN and is followed by NUL or '/', the loader reads past the end of the path buffer and writes past the end of a stack-allocated internal buffer.
statements.impact_statement: Exploitation needs a setuid or setgid binary whose DT_RPATH or DT_RUNPATH begins with $ORIGIN. None of the setuid/setgid binaries shipped in the Liquibase Secure image (su, passwd, mount, chsh and the other shadow and util-linux tools) contain $ORIGIN at all, and the container runs Liquibase as the unprivileged liquibase user.

statements.status_notes: The strncasecmp function in the GNU C Library 2.24 and later optimized for the Power8 architecture may read one byte beyond the input size limit, which may crash a program when that byte is not readable. This condition may happen when the input strings to the strncasecmp function are attacker controlled in an application and they match all the way up to the edge of their page and the neighbouring page is either not mapped or is not readable.
statements.impact_statement: The affected strncasecmp is the Power8-optimised assembly variant (sysdeps/powerpc/powerpc64/power8), which glibc selects only on ppc64 and ppc64le builds. The Liquibase Secure image is published for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 only, so the vulnerable routine is not compiled into the libc.so.6 it ships; the generic strncasecmp used on those architectures is not affected.
